PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.

1. Directory Verification:

2. Command Execution:

   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)

   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required

   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 14400000ms / 240 minutes, max 28800000ms / 8 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.

tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 28800000ms / 480 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 14400000ms (240 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 14400000ms / 240 minutes, max 28800000ms / 8 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

[package]
name = "gitcerberocraft"
version = "1.0.0"
edition = "2021"
description = "GitCerberoCraft - a free, graphical Git client with a CLI and MCP server"
default-run = "gitcerberocraft"

[lib]
name = "gcc_core"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "gitcerberocraft"
path = "src/main.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "gitcerberocraft-cli"
path = "src/bin/gitcerberocraft-cli.rs"

[dependencies]
eframe = { version = "0.29", default-features = false, features = ["default_fonts", "glow", "accesskit", "wayland", "x11"] }
egui-phosphor = "0.7"
git2 = { version = "0.19", default-features = false, features = ["https", "ssh", "vendored-libgit2"] }
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
ureq = { version = "2", features = ["json"] }
dirs = "5"
sys-locale = "0.3"
rfd = "0.15"
chrono = { version = "0.4", default-features = false, features = ["clock", "std"] }
image = { version = "0.25", default-features = false, features = ["png"] }
zip = { version = "2", default-features = false, features = ["deflate"] }

[target.'cfg(not(windows))'.dependencies]
git2 = { version = "0.19", default-features = false, features = ["https", "ssh", "vendored-libgit2", "vendored-openssl"] }

[profile.dev]
opt-level = 1

[profile.dev.package."*"]
opt-level = 2

input.content:
# GitCerberoCraft – behaviour and layout sheet

This is an application (a Git client), not a game, so there is no movement,
weapons or scoring. The "mechanics" are the layout sizes, colours, controls and
rules of each action. Values measured from the reference pictures are marked
`reference/picture-N`; everything else is **estimated** (clean room: the
original program was never opened).

## Window and layout
| Value | Number | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Default window size | 1232 × 760 | reference/picture-10..13 (window width) |
| Menu bar height | 24 px, colour #1F1F1F | reference/picture-11 (sampled) |
| Tab bar height | 36 px, colour #2A2D34, active tab #33373F | reference/picture-11 (sampled) |
| Repository toolbar height | 46 px, colour #33373F | reference/picture-12 (sampled) |
| Content background | #1C1E23 | reference/picture-11/12 (sampled) |
| Left panel width | 206 px, colour #272A31 | reference/picture-12 |
| Graph header height | 22 px, colour #272A31 | reference/picture-12 |
| Commit row height | 28 px | reference/picture-12 (rows at y 176/204/232) |
| Branch/Tag column | 140 px | reference/picture-12 |
| Graph column | 84 px minimum, +22 px per extra lane | reference/picture-3/12 |
| First lane centre | 36 px into the graph column | reference/picture-12 |
| Lane spacing | 22 px | reference/picture-3 |
| Commit node radius | 11 px (merge commits 6 px) | reference/picture-12; merge size estimated |
| Lane colours | #15A0BF, #0669F7, #8E00C2, then a rainbow | first three sampled from reference/picture-3; rest estimated |
| Row tint | lane colour at 14 % over the background | reference/picture-12 (#1B2B32 sampled) |
| Branch label | lane colour at 45 % | reference/picture-12 (#195F71 sampled) |
| Checked-out branch row (left panel) | #37553E with green check #5CB85C | reference/picture-10 (sampled) |
| Selected switch (List/Agents) | #2E3D5A | reference/picture-12 (sampled) |
| Status bar height | 24 px, colour #272A31 | reference/picture-11 |
| Dialog header / left list / selected | #3D424D / #32363F / #374665 | reference/picture-4 (sampled) |
| Clone and welcome pages background | #0D1017 | reference/picture-2/8 (sampled) |
| "Clone the repo!" button | #44088B | reference/picture-2 (sampled) |

## Controls
| Action | Key | Source |
|---|---|---|
| New tab / close / reopen | Ctrl+T / Ctrl+W / Ctrl+Shift+T | reference/picture-6 (File menu) |
| Clone / Init / Open repo | Ctrl+N / Ctrl+I / Ctrl+O | reference/picture-6 |
| Repo management | Alt+Ctrl+O | reference/picture-6 |
| External terminal / file manager | Alt+T / Alt+O | reference/picture-6 |
| Preferences | Ctrl+, | reference/picture-6 |
| Undo / Redo | Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y (also toolbar) | reference/picture-5 |
| Move selection in graph | Up / Down | estimated |
| Zoom | Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- / Ctrl+0, steps of 10 % | estimated |
| Checkout a branch | double-click | estimated |
| Context actions | right-click | estimated |

## Rules
- Pull button default: merge, fast-forward if possible; arrow menu offers Fetch All, fast-forward only, rebase (estimated).
- Push sets the upstream the first time; force push uses "with lease" and asks first.
- Undo covers: commit (soft reset, changes kept), checkout, branch create/delete, reset.
- The working tree is re-checked every 2.5 s; auto fetch is off by default (0 min).
- Graph shows at most 2000 commits by default (setting).
- Language folders are re-scanned every 2 s; a new `*.json` file appears automatically.
- Commit summary counter starts at 72 characters.
- AI diff limit: 60 000 characters sent per question.

content.text:
Ho creato GitCerberoCraft in Rust, con la stessa grafica dell'originale. Ci sono la barra delle schede e la pagina iniziale con Apri/Clona/Crea, la vista del repository con il grafo dei commit colorato, il pannello a sinistra (rami locali e remoti, stash, tag) e la barra degli strumenti (Annulla, Ripeti, Pull, Push, Branch, Stash, Pop, Terminale). Ci sono anche la pagina di clonazione, la finestra "Inizializza repository" e il menu del profilo. I nomi GitKraken, Trial e Upgrade non compaiono più da nessuna parte. Il controllo automatico è passato: il programma si compila, la schermata somiglia all'originale per circa l'83%, e la prova automatica riesce a muoversi nel grafo, mettere in stage le modifiche e fare un commit.

Ecco le altre cose che mi hai chiesto:
- **Riga di comando con server MCP:** una versione separata esegue fetch, pull, push, commit, branch, stash, merge e altro, e contiene il server MCP per gli agenti AI. Ho provato che il server risponde e che lo stato del repository e il fetch funzionano; un vero client AI collegato non l'ho ancora provato. In Preferenze trovi la configurazione pronta da incollare.
- **Lingue:** ci sono inglese e italiano. Se aggiungi un nuovo file di lingua, l'app lo trova da sola entro un paio di secondi e lo mette nell'elenco delle lingue. Questo è scritto ma non l'ho provato aggiungendo davvero un file.
- **AI:** puoi collegarla via API (Anthropic, servizi compatibili OpenAI, Ollama) oppure come agente ACP (per esempio Claude Code o Gemini CLI). Serve a spiegare un commit, rivedere le modifiche o scrivere il messaggio di commit. Non l'ho provata con un servizio vero, perché serve la tua chiave o un agente installato.
- **Scaricare Git:** l'app mostra le versioni ufficiali per il tuo sistema e te le fa scegliere; su Windows puoi prendere l'installer, la versione portatile o quella compatta. Non ho provato un download reale.

Sul tuo computer Git non è installato, quindi ho messo nell'app un motore Git integrato: funziona anche senza. Per pull con rebase, Git LFS e gestori di credenziali conviene comunque scaricare Git dalle Preferenze.

In più ho aggiunto un terminale integrato, il Launchpad con lo stato di tutti i repository recenti, il fetch automatico e più profili per il commit.

Restano due cose: i pannelli che si aprono cliccando un commit o le modifiche in corso, e la pagina Preferenze, li ho disegnati io perché nessuna delle tue immagini li mostra. Il controllo automatico confronta solo l'aspetto delle schermate, non tutto il comportamento dell'app. Come prossimo passo, se mi mandi una foto dell'originale con un commit selezionato o con delle modifiche in corso, posso rendere quei pannelli identici.
